newsitem.title: INDIA: India palm oil imports may exceed one mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: India palm oil imports may exceed one mln tonnes.

text.p: Indian palm oil imports this year are projected to exceed one million tonnes, almost matching China's, a visiting Malaysian trade official said on Thursday.
"We are very optimistic that India will take at least one million tonnes this year," Mohammed Hashim, chief executive officer of the Malaysian Palm Oil Promotion Council (MPOPC), told reporters.
With population growth of 2.1 percent against China's one percent, India would soon match or even surpass China as a palm oil importer, he added.

"India's per capita consumption of palm oil is 6.7 kg against 10 kg for China," Hashim said. "The World Health Organisation recommends oil consumption levels of around 20 to 24 kg per capita. So there is lot of opportunity to grow more."
Hashim was speaking ahead of a four-day promotion programme the MPOPC plans to start in Bombay on Friday.
Though India ranks third among the world's producers of edible oil, it has a a huge shortfall, the MPOPC said.
"With the per capita consumption growing at about six percent per annum due to the increasing population and better purchasing power, this gap is guaranteed to widen," the MPOPC said in a statement.
Malaysia is the world's largest producer of palm oil, with output of 7.8 million tonnes last year, or 52 percent of world production, Hashim said.

India, which buys about 80 percent of its palm oil from Malaysia, imported 680,000 tonnes of palm oil up to August 31 this year, compared to the 750,000 tonnes the country imported in 1995, Hashim said.
Pakistan imported 1.1 million tonnes of palm oil last year, with China importing around one million tonnes.

Indian traders said earlier this week that they expected the country would import an additional 350,000 tonnes of palm olein in September and October. Palm olein is a refined, bleached and deodorised form of palm oil.
